methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Carbyon is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Hans De Neve that has raised €22.3M to date. The comparable universe consists of 9 peers within the Climate & Energy sector, including 1 public company (Lenza, ticker LNZA) and 8 private firms. Notable private peers include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable to Carbyon. The dataset contains insufficient narrow-stage comparables: zero same-stage Series A peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-valuation-tier companies were identified within the Climate & Energy sector. A meaningful peer-median requires a minimum of three comparable datapoints; this threshold cannot be met through stage- or tier-filtered subsets. Attempting to derive valuation multiples from the broader all-sector peer set would introduce unacceptable methodological bias given the heterogeneity of business models and capital intensity across the Climate & Energy landscape.

The analysis does not yield a supported valuation range or triangulated conclusion. Valuation of Carbyon would require alternative methods not present in the available dataset—such as DCF modeling, revenue multiple analysis from differently-screened comparables, or investor round data—to establish defensible benchmarks. The primary uncertainty is the absence of granular financial metrics (revenue, EBITDA, cash burn) and narrowly comparable transaction precedents at the same development stage.
